Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC DoS based on ASN.1 decoder read overrun
Vulnerabilities.Description: In all released versions of MIT krb5, an unauthenticated attacker can cause a KDC process to perform a large read overrun, likely causing the process to terminate.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS in RPCSEC_GSS buffer decode failure
Vulnerabilities.Description: The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4 and later do not free partially decoded buffers on failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS messages.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak DoS in xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure
Vulnerabilities.Description: xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated memory leak DoS in KDB keytab key decryption error path
Vulnerabilities.Description: krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly trigger key decryption failures.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated DoS exploiting dereference of null policy name pointers
Vulnerabilities.Description: The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a policy request with an empty policy name that reaches authorization checks or logging code.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion DoS via unbounded RPC XDR allocation
Vulnerabilities.Description: The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded memory allocations during XDR decoding.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via GSS-RPC auth flavor switching
Vulnerabilities.Description: The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT error paths
Vulnerabilities.Description: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger authentication failures.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated CPU DoS via AUTH_GSSAPI client states cleanup
Vulnerabilities.Description: clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests
Vulnerabilities.Description: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests. Each failed request allocates client state that is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout, allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it is reclaimed.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: kadmind: request alteration and protected information disclosure
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.4 and later, an active network attacker can alter the arguments sent by a legitimate client to RPC services protected by RPCSEC_GSS, or cause return values to be sent in plain text.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 KDC unauthenticated CPU DoS via quadratic ASN.1 SEQUENCE OF decoding
Vulnerabilities.Description: decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded element array one entry at a time, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field over TCP.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT Kerberos 5: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference in NegoEx mechanism
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) before 1.22.3, there is a NULL pointer dereference if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger this, causing the process to terminate in parse_nego_message.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5): Denial of Service via integer underflow and out-of-bounds read
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) before 1.22.3, there is an integer underflow and resultant out-of-bounds read if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger this, possibly causing the process to terminate in parse_message.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Alteration of authentication indicators in CAMMAC container
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.14 and later (since authentication indicator support was added), an authenticated attacker can bypass authentication indicator requirements using an unkeyed checksum in the CAMMAC authdata container.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Unauthenticated KDC NULL pointer dereference KDC DoS via crafted PKINIT pre-auth request
Vulnerabilities.Description: If a KDC is configured to allow PKINIT authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference, causing the process to terminate.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via malformed PAC in S4U2Proxy requests
Vulnerabilities.Description: MIT krb5 through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the KDC's get_pac_princ_with_realm() that returns success while leaving the client principal NULL on malformed names. A malicious or compromised cross-realm trusted KDC can send an S4U2Proxy request with a PAC carrying a malformed client name to crash krb5kdc and deny authentication.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: krb5: Denial of Service via crafted forwarded credentials
Vulnerabilities.Description: MIT Kerberos 5 (krb5) through 1.22.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference in make_cred_list() in rd_cred.c that allows authenticated Kerberos clients to crash services by sending mismatched KRB-CRED arrays. Attackers can send forwarded credentials with more tickets than ticket_info entries through gss_accept_sec_context() to crash GSS-API acceptor services, causing denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Unauthorized key reset of protected principal via kpasswd
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.15 and later, a client with kadmin administrative privileges can bypass the lockdown_keys attribute by using the password change protocol instead of the kadmin protocol.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: Improper authorization via flawed PAC checksum verification
Vulnerabilities.Description: In MIT krb5 release 1.21 and later, server applications will erroneously treat the PAC within a ticket as verified when the server checksum is invalid.

Vulnerabilities.Title: krb5: MIT krb5 GSS-RPC client memory leak on XID mismatch retries
Vulnerabilities.Description: clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by triggering authentication retries.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffe ...
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer vulnerability in OSGeo gdal (frmts/zlib/contrib/infback9 modules). This vulnerability is associated with program files inftree9.C‎.

This issue affects gdal: before 3.11.0.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip missing checks on symbolic link extraction
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When extracting a tar archive pip may not check symbolic links point into the extraction directory if the tarfile module doesn't implement PEP 706.
Note that upgrading pip to a "fixed" version for this vulnerability doesn't fix all known vulnerabilities that are remediated by using a Python version that implements PEP 706.

Note that this is a vulnerability in pip's fallback implementation of tar extraction for Python versions that don't implement PEP 706
and therefore are not secure to all vulnerabilities in the Python 'tarfile' module. If you're using a Python version that implements PEP 706
then pip doesn't use the "vulnerable" fallback code.

Mitigations include upgrading to a version of pip that includes the fix, upgrading to a Python version that implements PEP 706 (Python >=3.9.17, >=3.10.12, >=3.11.4, or >=3.12),
applying the linked patch, or inspecting source distributions (sdists) before installation as is already a best-practice.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Arbitrary file installation via malicious package indexes
Vulnerabilities.Description:
pip would incorrectly handle doubly-encoded package URLs from indexes allowing for files to be installed to arbitrary locations on disk even when installing wheels.




This vulnerability requires downloading or installing a package from a malicious package index to succeed, malicious packages alone are not able to exploit this vulnerability. Note that this vulnerability only materially impacts users running `pip download` with the `--only-binary` option as installing source distributions from an untrusted index is already an unsafe operation that executes code during install time.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Incorrect file installation due to improper archive handling
Vulnerabilities.Description: pip handles concatenated tar and ZIP files as ZIP files regardless of filename or whether a file is both a tar and ZIP file. This behavior could result in confusing installation behavior, such as installing "incorrect" files according to the filename of the archive. New behavior only proceeds with installation if the file identifies uniquely as a ZIP or tar archive, not as both.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Arbitrary code execution or information disclosure via malicious wheel package installation
Vulnerabilities.Description: pip prior to version 26.1 would run self-update check functionality after installing wheel files which required importing well-known Python modules names. These module imports were intentionally deferred to increase startup time of the pip CLI. The patch changes self-update functionality to run before wheels are installed to prevent newly-installed modules from being imported shortly after the installation of a wheel package. Users should still review package contents prior to installation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: python-pip: Path traversal via malicious entry point name in pip wheel installation allows arbitrary file overwrite
Vulnerabilities.Description: pip would treat console_scripts and gui_scripts as paths instead of file names without sanitizing the resolved absolute path to the installation directory, leading to entry points being installed outside the installation directory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: pip: pip: Information disclosure via path traversal when installing crafted wheel archives
Vulnerabilities.Description: When pip is installing and extracting a maliciously crafted wheel archive, files may be extracted outside the installation directory. The path traversal is limited to prefixes of the installation directory, thus isn't able to inject or overwrite executable files in typical situations.
